name: Tension testing of structural alloys fully submerged in liquid helium (ASTM E1450, 4 K, strain rate <= 1e-3 s-1)
plain_name: Pull a metal test bar apart while it sits in liquid helium
description: Standard tensile test (yield strength, tensile strength, elongation, reduction of area) of structural alloys with the specimen fully submerged in normal liquid helium (He I) inside a cryostat, under crosshead displacement control at a nominal strain rate of 1e-3 s-1 or less. The standard designates the test temperature 4 K (He I boils at 4.2 K at sea level, 4.0 K at 1677 m).
keywords: Pull a metal test bar apart while it sits in liquid helium

sources.citation: ASTM E1450-92(1998), Standard Test Method for Tension Testing of Structural Alloys in Liquid Helium, ASTM International, DOI 10.1520/E1450-92R98 (scope as published on the ASTM store page; accessed 2026-11-01)

requirements.rationale: The specimen must be fully submerged in a normal liquid-helium (He I) bath; a dry or conduction-cooled stage does not satisfy the method.
The test temperature is the He I boiling point, 4.2 K at sea level (4.0 K at 1677 m); the sample space must reach it.
A tension load train acting on the specimen inside the cryostat is required (special apparatus for cryogenic tension testing).

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
